title: [YouPass Collect] - Australian tourism trends 1995-2005
prompt: The bar chart below shows how tourism to Australia from three different countries changed between 1995 and 2005. The line chart illustrates the types of stay that tourists chose during the same period. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the number of tourists visiting Australia from three countries between 1995 and 2005, while the line graph illustrates changes in accommodation preferences during the same period.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, tourism from the UK and USA rose significantly, whereas Japanese visitor numbers declined. Regarding accommodation, backpacking gained popularity throughout the period, while hotel stays fluctuated, with both types of accommodation attracting equal numbers by 2005.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at tourist arrivals, in 1995, Japan led with 1,450,000 visitors, nearly double the UK's 800,000 and almost triple the USA's 500,000. Over the following decade, Japanese tourism experienced a substantial decline, falling to 1,100,000 by 2005. In contrast, both UK and USA visitor numbers surged dramatically, with each country reaching 1,500,000 tourists in 2005, representing increases of 700,000 and 1,000,000 respectively.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding accommodation choices, hotel stays dominated in 1995 at 1,750,000, significantly outnumbering backpackers at just 300,000. Subsequently, the hotel category peaked at 2,500,000 in 2000 before plummeting by half its peak to 1,250,000 by 2005. Conversely, backpacking demonstrated steady growth throughout the period, rising from its initial figure to 900,000 in 2000, and ultimately reaching 1,250,000 in the final year, thereby equaling hotel accommodations.
